clue.text: Toy rattled, interrupting father with a variable routine

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters go inside another word
something rattled is shaken about, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be jumbled
an everyday word for a father
taken as written
x, y and z are the usual algebra letters for unknowns

explanation.surface: A child shakes a toy, interrupting a father whose daily routine is anything but fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled toy sits between the second and third letters of DAD, then A and Y follow to give DAY-TO-DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Day-to-day describes the ordinary, everyday business of life, which is exactly a routine.

clue.text: Chain of islands completely enthralling first pair of tourists

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: all means completely, as in all gone

indicators.note: a first pair means just the opening two letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: the opening two letters of tourists

explanation.surface: A string of islands so lovely that it captivates every arriving tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or group of low islands enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Film in which Alec Guinness appeared sinister in dark style he developed

definitions.text: Film in which Alec Guinness appeared

indicators.note: in places one word within the other letters
a style that is developed is worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
ill can mean evil or malevolent, as in ill intent

explanation.surface: A film buff notes Alec Guinness looked menacing in a dark manner he crafted for the role.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about acting; in fact sinister gives ILL, which goes inside the rearranged letters of dark style he.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ladykillers (1955) is the Ealing comedy in which Guinness starred as a gang leader.

clue.text: Single saint taken in by attractive fraud

indicators.note: something taken in by another is swallowed up inside it

parts.note: dishy is British slang for good-looking
single means one
the usual abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A lone saint is duped by a charming swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: Dishy is informal British slang for good-looking; the single and the saint sit inside it, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is deceitful behaviour, and dishonesty is the general noun for such deceit.

clue.text: During party a psychiatrist talks annoyingly

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: found running across the end of party, a, and the start of psychiatrist

explanation.surface: At a party, a psychiatrist chatters on tiresomely.
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to talk shrilly and incessantly, like a small dog barking.

clue.text: Revolutionary plans for unwanted messages

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read from the other end

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Plans for an uprising are sent out as junk email.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the name for unsolicited bulk email or messages sent indiscriminately.

clue.text: Worked up prior to producing medley

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or reshaped, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone got agitated before putting together a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Worked up looks like one phrase meaning agitated, but worked alone is the signal and up prior to is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixed collection of things, such as a medley of tunes or scented petals.

clue.text: Start of research into state of the sea

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the word that follows

parts.note: Maine is a US state

indicators.note: the start of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of research

explanation.surface: The beginning of a study into the condition of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: State of the sea reads as condition, but state is Maine, and of the sea is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine is the adjective for anything relating to or found in the sea.

clue.text: Composer having bad manners has job capturing hearts

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so one letter joins the other letters
bad means faulty or disordered, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A musician with rude manners holds down a job that wins people over.
explanation.walkthrough: Capturing hearts reads as winning affection, but hearts is just H added to the letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was the nineteenth-century German composer of symphonies and the German Requiem.

clue.text: Five hundred wander in herd

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: Five hundred animals roam together as a herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd or flock of animals being driven as a body.

clue.text: Go and catch editor up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to trap is to catch
the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and grab the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave or go away.

clue.text: Great round left for fan

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: super means great
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A fine round of drinks set aside for a devoted follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter is a follower or fan of a team or cause.

clue.text: Spot temperature after dance party

indicators.note: after says the word before it is placed behind the words that follow it

parts.note: the polka is a lively dance
a do is a party
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Someone notices the temperature after a dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads temperature first, but it ends the answer; the dance and the party come before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A polka dot is one of a pattern of round spots on fabric.

clue.text: Dark colour in strand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a deep brownish-crimson shade
second meaning: to leave someone stranded, as on a desert island

explanation.surface: A dark colour woven into a strand of thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Maroon names a brownish red, and as a verb means to abandon someone somewhere isolated.

clue.text: Encounters room on island, quiet in upper regions

indicators.note: in puts the run of short pieces inside the longer word

parts.note: the skies are the upper regions of the air
RM is the abbreviation for room
I is the abbreviation for island
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Clashes over accommodation on an island, with silence on the upper floors.
explanation.walkthrough: On here only joins room and island in sequence; it is not a position signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirmishes are brief fights, the minor encounters between small forces.

clue.text: Study, keen, or cry desperately for calculation aid

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: acting desperately means acting wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A student, eager or wailing in despair, needs help with sums.
explanation.walkthrough: A ready reckoner is a printed book or table of precalculated figures, once common in British shops and offices.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a reference of worked-out sums used to save doing arithmetic, so an aid to calculation.

clue.text: Purpose in elevated novel, not heartless fun

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the other
in a down entry, elevated means lifted up, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: Emma is the Jane Austen novel
a use is a purpose, as in what is the use

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of not

explanation.surface: A lofty novel has a point but is not without its lighter side.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the book Emma, turned upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is enjoyment or entertainment, the state of being entertained by something funny.

clue.text: Old article about northern programme

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the next letter goes inside

parts.note: aged means old
a is the indefinite article
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: An old article about the north that sets out a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: AGED and A together go round N, which sits between the third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a schedule or programme for a meeting.

clue.text: Dull name carried by blend not working

indicators.note: something carried by another is held inside it

parts.note: to unite is to join or blend together
N is the abbreviation for name
someone resting, especially an actor, is out of work

explanation.surface: A boring brand-name product sold in a blend that fails to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Resting is the polite theatre word for an actor between jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninteresting means failing to hold attention, a plain synonym of dull.

clue.text: Give answer following crossing

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a ford is a shallow river crossing

explanation.surface: Supply a reply after going over the way across.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford is to provide or supply, as in the view affords a glimpse of the sea.

clue.text: Cook accepting fish willingly

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to fry is to cook
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A chef happily takes in a fish to prepare.
explanation.definitionFit: Freely means without compulsion, of one's own accord, which is doing something willingly.

clue.text: Element in mobile ringtone

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some feature found in a mobile phone's ringtone.
explanation.walkthrough: Mobile reads as the phone, but it is the anagram signal working on ringtone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a chemical element, the gas making up most of the air.

clue.text: Understanding finally about live bird

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of understanding
re means about, concerning
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Coming to understand, at last, something about a living bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A grebe is a diving waterbird with lobed toes, such as the great crested grebe.

clue.text: Settled softly with relief

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
aid is relief or help

explanation.surface: Someone sank quietly back, relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is settled has been paid in full.

clue.text: Go too far across section of river

parts.note: over can mean across, as in over the road
a reach is a straight stretch of river

explanation.surface: Travelling too far over a stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach is to stretch beyond one's capacity, going further than is wise.

clue.text: Carnivore has endlessly consuming hunger

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter
consuming means swallowing, so the next word goes inside

parts.note: has minus its final letter
a yen is a longing or hunger

explanation.surface: A meat-eater with a bottomless appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a meat-eating African mammal that hunts and scavenges.

clue.text: Responsibility for tax

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a moral or legal obligation
second meaning: a levy on goods, as in customs charges

explanation.definitionFit: A duty is both an obligation one must fulfil and a charge levied on imports.

clue.text: Botched raid's set to be calamity

indicators.note: botched means done clumsily, so the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bungled raid is heading for ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden catastrophe causing great damage, matching calamity.
